s1.syndrome_frame: Acute cardiac syndrome with inflammatory and thrombotic features
salient_findings: Elevated cardiac markers (troponin and brain natriuretic peptide)
key_facts: 47-year-old man with no significant medical history
Exposure to COVID-19 through family member 12 days before death
Developed general malaise without fever or respiratory symptoms 2 days before death
Fatigue worsened over time, and patient was unable to eat the day before death
Patient was not vaccinated
Cardiopulmonary arrest occurred during transport to hospital
No coronary artery sclerosis or stenosis was observed
Elevated inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β and IL-6)
SARS-CoV-2 antigen test positive (>5000 pg/mL) from oropharyngeal swab
Postmortem CT scan showed dorsal pulmonary infiltrative shadow and bilateral pleural effusions
Pericardial effusion of 70 mL clear fluid
Heart weight was 426g, above normal range
Lung weights were above normal range

differentials: Acute coronary syndrome with embolic features
per_call: Acute coronary syndrome with embolic features

shortlist.label: Myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated cardiac markers, diffuse contraction band necrosis, and lymphocytes in cardiac muscle

shortlist.label: COVID-19 associated myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: SARS-CoV-2 antigen test positive and exposure to COVID-19 through family member

shortlist.label: Pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Pericardial effusion of 70 mL clear fluid and elevated inflammatory cytokines

shortlist.label: Fulminant myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Cardiopulmonary arrest occurred during transport to hospital and heart weight was above normal range

shortlist.label: COVID-19 associated pericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Pericardial effusion and positive SARS-CoV-2 antigen test

raw.rationale: The patient's recent exposure to COVID-19, lack of vaccination, and presence of SARS-CoV-2 antigen, combined with the histological findings of diffuse contraction band necrosis and platelet aggregation in cardiac microvessels, strongly support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Myocarditis
rejected.why: Too general, as the patient's condition is specifically linked to COVID-19

rejected.label: Pericarditis
rejected.why: Although pericardial effusion was present, the primary issue seems to be myocardial involvement

rejected.label: Fulminant myocarditis
rejected.why: While the condition was severe, the specific link to COVID-19 makes 'COVID-19 associated myocarditis' more precise

rejected.label: COVID-19 associated pericarditis
rejected.why: The primary findings suggest myocardial involvement rather than pericardial disease as the main issue
